title: Data Analytics
tagline: Turning data into evidence for better decisions.
overview: Data Analytics is one of the most accessible modern career paths for a Statistics graduate. A data analyst takes raw or semi-structured information, investigates it, identifies patterns and trends, communicates findings, and helps an organisation make better decisions. The industry can change, but the analytical foundation travels with you.
reality_check: Good analytics is not simply 'Put data into Excel and make a chart.' The statistical foundation matters. An analyst needs to understand variation, distributions, relationships, sampling, uncertainty, and the crucial difference between an apparent pattern and a meaningful, statistically significant one.

title: Data Science
formula: Probability & Inference + Scientific Programming + Predictive Modeling
overview: Data Science goes beyond describing what happened in the past. It investigates: What is likely to happen next? What underlying factors explain it? Can we predict it? Can we build a self-contained system that learns systematically from historical data? This is where classical Statistics intersects vigorously with computational computer science and machine learning.
reality_check: A Statistics degree does NOT automatically make you a Data Scientist. Statistics gives you the mathematical intuition and inference rigor, but you must deliberately build the computational, algorithmic, and software engineering layer outside lectures.

title: Machine Learning & Artificial Intelligence
tagline: The mathematical foundation beneath modern artificial intelligence.
formula: Probability & Linear Algebra + Algorithms + Neural Frameworks + Software Engineering
overview: Modern AI systems depend heavily on data. Machine learning involves algorithms learning patterns from massive datasets to make automated decisions or generate outputs. Statistics is what helps you understand what happens beneath the predictions: estimation, bias vs. variance, loss functions, uncertainty, and mathematical generalisation.
reality_check: Statistics gives you the mathematical reason why models converge, but serious ML Engineering requires software engineering discipline: object-oriented programming, data structures, algorithm complexity, Docker containers, APIs, and cloud systems knowledge. You cannot just import a library; you must engineer production-grade systems.

You need to understand economic indicators, financial statements, balance sheets, and regulatory frameworks (Basel accords, IFRS 9) alongside your statistical models.

tagline: The mathematical science of long-term risk and solvency.
formula: Probability Distributions + Actuarial Mathematics + Life Contingencies + Financial Theory
overview: Insurance is fundamentally about uncertainty, mortality, catastrophic events, and systemic risk. reality_check: A university degree in Statistics gives you an incredible head-start, but becoming a fully certified Actuary requires passing rigorous professional examinations (IFoA in the UK, SOA in the USA, or CIA). It is a demanding, prestigious, highly paid profession that requires commitment to lifelong credentialing.

reality_check: Economics is not physics; you cannot easily run laboratory experiments on entire national economies. Econometricians must master observational causal inference: instrumental variables, difference-in-differences, and panel data methods to isolate true economic mechanisms.

title: Agriculture & Environment
tagline: Critical for Africa's future: food security, climate science, and geospatial modeling.
formula: Agronomic Experiments + Spatial Statistics + Climate Data + Remote Sensing
overview: Agriculture remains the backbone of the African economy, while climate change poses an urgent existential challenge. Statistics supports agricultural field trials, crop yield predictions, soil nutrient modeling, flood risk mapping, and food-security surveillance. When Statistics is paired with GIS and remote sensing, it becomes a powerful geospatial science.
reality_check: In agricultural experiments, crops don't grow in sterile laboratories. They are subject to soil heterogeneity, rainfall fluctuations, and pest infestations. Classical experimental design (RCBD, Split-Plot, Factorial) was literally invented in agriculture to solve these exact real-world challenges.

title: Genomics & Bioinformatics
tagline: Decoding the human genome with high-dimensional statistical computing.
formula: High-Dimensional Statistics + Molecular Biology + Bio-computing + Next-Gen Sequencing
overview: Modern biological research produces massive datasets: billions of DNA base pairs, RNA expressions across thousands of cells, and complex gene networks. Genomics and bioinformatics use high-dimensional Statistics, multiple hypothesis testing corrections, and machine learning to identify disease-causing genetic mutations and design targeted molecular therapies.
reality_check: In genomics, you often have 20,000 genes measured for only 100 patient samples — the classical 'p >> n' curse of dimensionality. Standard naive statistics collapses. You must master false discovery rates (FDR), regularization, and high-dimensional matrix methods to discover true biological signals.
